text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Greek Cypriot newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United Nations and other countries are exerting pressure for a dialogue between Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots.
- State's 1997 budgets are to be presented to the House of Representatives on Thursday.
- Russian fugitives were sent back to Russia yesterday.
- Rumours of Turkish attempts to cause friction along the ceasefire line cause panic.
- The government is trying to bring back unconstitutional legislation to ban strikes.
- Limassol and Paphos went up in smoke yesterday from forest fires.
- Washington approaches the military in Ankara to avert possibility of a Turkish strike against the Cyprus National Guard military installations.
- Police suspect murderers of pub owner found dead on Friday were paid killers from abroad.
- A post mortem will solve the mystery surrounding the death of a Yugoslavian found dead in his car last week.
- Climate of uncertainty surrounds outcome of Greek elections.
- President Glafcos Clerides starts contacts with trade unions on payment of cost of living allowance.
- Dozens flock to home of 81-year-old woman who says she saw the Virgin Mary and Apostle Andrew.
